claims.object_text: accumulation of double-strand breaks in patients' brain genome
claims.quote: the activity, but not the protein level, of an essential DNA repair enzyme, polynucleotide kinase 3'-phosphatase (PNKP), is severely abrogated in both HD and SCA3 resulting in accumulation of double-strand breaks in patients' brain genome.
we observed that PNKP interacts with the nuclear isoform of 6-phosphofructo-2-kinase fructose-2,6-bisphosphatase 3 (PFKFB3).
Depletion of PFKFB3 markedly abrogates PNKP activity without changing its protein level.
Supplementation of F2,6BP restored PNKP activity in the nuclear extracts of patients' brain.
Moreover, intracellular delivery of F2,6BP restored both the activity of PNKP and the integrity of transcribed genome in neuronal cells derived from the striatum of the HD mouse.

claims.object_text: F2,6BP as in vivo cofactor for PNKP
claims.quote: Importantly, supplementing F2,6BP rescued the HD phenotype in Drosophila, suggesting F2,6BP to serve in vivo as a cofactor for the proper functionality of PNKP and thereby, of brain health.
